title: NY State Senate · District 34
area: Northeast Bronx (Co-op City, Pelham Bay, Throggs Neck, City Island) and parts of southern Westchester County (Pelham, Pelham Manor).

context.text: Both major-party primaries for this seat were canceled; incumbent Nathalia Fernandez advanced on the Democratic and Working Families lines and Adrian Romero advanced on the Conservative line without appearing on a primary ballot.

candidates.name: Nathalia Fernandez
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 34 (since January 2023)

summary.text: Nathalia Fernandez is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for re-election to New York State Senate District 34. She has represented the district since January 2023 and previously served in the State Assembly representing District 80 from 2018 to 2023.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in public relations from Hofstra University in 2010.
Worked as an administrative assistant at Genesis Realty Group and as executive coordinator and chief of staff to Assemblymember Mark Gjonaj before running for office.
Served as a Bronx regional representative in the office of Governor Andrew Cuomo.
Represented the 80th Assembly District from 2018 to 2023, including winning a 2018 special election, before moving to the State Senate.
Chairs the Senate Alcoholism and Substance Use Disorders Committee and co-chairs the Joint Senate Task Force on Opioids, Addiction and Overdose Prevention.

priorities.text: "I want to build resiliency for our coastal communities, increase transit access, funding for our schools and bring good paying jobs to uplift our local economy."

"Climate change is a constant concern for this area. Our coastal communities are threatened and our roads and transit systems often flood. We need to build long term resilience for this district through investing in infrastructure that stays strong against climate change and providing homeowners with assistance to protect their property."
"The East Bronx is a transportation desert... I want to make that a reality. We need transit access to connect our communities and continue to build economic growth for the area."

"I have a history of championing small businesses... I will do this through addressing the high property taxes that are getting in the way of their growth and honor the diversity of this district through uplifting minority and women owned businesses."

positions.summary: Voted yes on the GREAT Act (S9500-A), which passed the Senate 39–21 and establishes a virtual power plant program and incentives for distributed energy resources to reduce energy costs and grid strain.
Voted yes on S8455-B, which passed the Senate 35–25 and creates new criminal offenses restricting the sale of flare guns.
Sponsored S10149, which would eliminate insurance preauthorization requirements for outpatient substance use disorder treatment.

record.text: Sponsored S10156-B, establishing a school speed-zone camera demonstration program in the Village of Pelham; signed by the Governor August 14, 2026 (Chapter 216).

Sponsored S10632, which would prohibit a victim's voluntary intoxication from being used as a defense to a sex-crime charge; passed the Senate 60–0 on June 4, 2026 and remained in the Assembly Codes Committee.
Sponsored S10149, which would remove preauthorization requirements for outpatient substance use disorder treatment coverage; in Senate Insurance Committee as of April 30, 2026.

candidates.name: Adrian Romero
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced to the general election on the Conservative Party line without appearing on a primary ballot; did not appear on the Republican primary ballot.

summary.text: Adrian Romero is running for New York State Senate District 34 on the Conservative Party line against incumbent Nathalia Fernandez.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, public statements, or completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey were found for Adrian Romero as of September 2026. Ballotpedia has not compiled biographical details or campaign-finance data for him.
